subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core execution anti-drift enforcement layer for artifact-gated status and post-verification idle handling, or keep this limited to existing loop/stall diagnostics until concrete reproductions justify more enforcement?
rationale: The request would add policy, timing, config, telemetry, and persistent state behavior across core agent execution, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or false-positive tolerance.

options.title: Keep open for scoped design
options.body: Treat this as a product/runtime design item and ask for concrete repro evidence before deciding which guard subset belongs in core.

options.title: Narrow to existing guardrails
options.body: Convert the remaining work into smaller issues for loop detection, stuck-session diagnostics, or strict-agentic gaps that can each be tested independently.

options.title: Decline broad enforcement
options.body: Close after maintainer decision if the team prefers current diagnostics and model/tool contracts over a new status-gating layer.

recommendation.title: Keep open for scoped design
recommendation.body: Treat this as a product/runtime design item and ask for concrete repro evidence before deciding which guard subset belongs in core.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the most recent current-main history for the nearby loop-detection, strict-agentic, and stuck-session documentation surfaces.
